title: MAHARASHTRA CLASS 11 — Biology | Biological Classification Five Kingdoms
description: Subject-wise test on Biological Classification Five Kingdoms (Biology) for MAHARASHTRA CLASS 11. 40Q.
subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a criterion used by R.H. Whittaker for the Five Kingdom Classification?

options.explanation: Cell structure is one of the criteria used by R.H. Whittaker for the Five Kingdom Classification.
Thallus organization is one of the criteria used by R.H. Whittaker for the Five Kingdom Classification.
Mode of nutrition is one of the criteria used by R.H. Whittaker for the Five Kingdom Classification.
Habitat is not a criterion used by R.H. Whittaker for the Five Kingdom Classification.

questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker's five-kingdom classification was based on five main criteria: cell structure, thallus organization (body organization), mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships. Habitat was not a primary criterion.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera are exclusively:

options.explanation: Kingdom Monera organisms are prokaryotic, not eukaryotic.
While some Monera form colonies, they are not truly multicellular.
Kingdom Monera organisms are indeed unicellular and prokaryotic.
Kingdom Monera organisms are not multicellular or eukaryotic.

questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera comprises all prokaryotic organisms. Most are unicellular, though some form colonies or filaments. They lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following structures is characteristic of organisms in Kingdom Fungi?

options.explanation: Fungi cell walls are typically made of chitin, not cellulose.
Fungi lack chloroplasts.
Fungi are indeed heterotrophic, obtaining nutrients as saprophytes or parasites.
While some primitive fungi have flagellated spores, it's not a universal characteristic of Kingdom Fungi.

questions.explanation: Fungi are primarily heterotrophic, obtaining nutrients as saprophytes (decomposers) or parasites. Their cell walls are typically made of chitin, they lack chloroplasts, and while some primitive fungi have flagellated spores, it's not a universal characteristic.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Diatoms and desmids (golden algae) are examples of organisms found in which kingdom?

options.explanation: Diatoms and desmids are eukaryotic, not prokaryotic like Monera.
Diatoms and desmids are indeed found in Kingdom Protista.
Diatoms and desmids are not fungi; they are photosynthetic and eukaryotic.
Diatoms and desmids are unicellular and not classified under Kingdom Plantae.

questions.explanation: Diatoms and desmids belong to Chrysophytes, which are a group under Kingdom Protista. They are eukaryotic, mostly photosynthetic, and unicellular.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: A scientist observes a single-celled organism under a microscope. It has a well-defined nucleus, chloroplasts, and a flagellum for locomotion. This organism most likely belongs to:

options.explanation: Monera are prokaryotic and lack a well-defined nucleus.
Fungi lack chloroplasts and are not typically flagellated.
The described characteristics match those of certain Protista, like Euglenoids.
Plantae are typically multicellular and not single-celled with a flagellum.

questions.explanation: The presence of a well-defined nucleus (eukaryotic), chloroplasts (photosynthetic), and a flagellum (motility) in a single-celled organism is characteristic of certain members of Kingdom Protista, such as Euglenoids. Monera are prokaryotic, Fungi lack chloroplasts, and Plantae are typically multicellular.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Fungi is INCORRECT?

options.explanation: Fungi are indeed heterotrophic.

options.text: Their cell walls are composed of chitin.
options.explanation: Fungi cell walls are indeed made of chitin.

options.text: They can reproduce sexually and asexually.
options.explanation: Fungi do reproduce both sexually and asexually.
Fungi typically store food as glycogen and oil, not starch.

questions.explanation: Fungi are indeed heterotrophic, have chitin cell walls, and reproduce both sexually and asexually. However, they typically store food reserves in the form of glycogen and oil, not starch. Starch is the primary storage carbohydrate in plants.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Cyanobacteria are often referred to as blue-green algae. Reason (R): They are photosynthetic prokaryotes that contain chlorophyll a similar to green plants.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason does correctly explain why cyanobacteria are called blue-green algae.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are indeed called blue-green algae due to their appearance and photosynthetic ability. They are prokaryotic (Monera) but possess chlorophyll 'a', making their photosynthesis similar to that of eukaryotic plants. The reason correctly explains why they are called 'blue-green algae' despite being prokaryotes.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which group of Protista is characterized by having a protein-rich layer called a pellicle instead of a cell wall, and shows both autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition?

options.explanation: Dinoflagellates have stiff cellulose plates, not a pellicle.
Diatoms have silica shells, not a pellicle.
Euglenoids have a flexible pellicle and exhibit both autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition.
Slime moulds are saprophytic or parasitic and do not have a pellicle.

questions.explanation: Euglenoids, such as _Euglena_, lack a rigid cell wall and instead have a flexible pellicle. They are photosynthetic in the presence of light (autotrophic) but become heterotrophic by predating on other small organisms in the absence of light.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Consider the following characteristics: I. Presence of a true nucleus. II. Unicellular organization. III. Cell wall made of chitin. IV. Absorptive mode of nutrition. An organism exhibiting characteristics I, III, and IV, but NOT II, would most likely belong to:

options.explanation: The presence of a true nucleus excludes Monera.
Most Protista are unicellular, which does not match the 'NOT II' condition.
The combination of a true nucleus, chitin cell wall, and absorptive nutrition in a multicellular organism fits Kingdom Fungi.
Plantae have cell walls made of cellulose, not chitin, and do not have absorptive nutrition like fungi.

questions.explanation: I. True nucleus: Excludes Monera. II. Unicellular organization: The question states 'NOT II', meaning it's multicellular. This excludes most Protista (which are unicellular eukaryotes). III. Cell wall made of chitin: This is a defining feature of Fungi. IV. Absorptive mode of nutrition: Also characteristic of Fungi.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the classification status of viruses?

options.text: Viruses are placed in Kingdom Monera due to their simple structure.
options.explanation: Viruses are not placed in any of the five kingdoms due to their non-cellular nature.

options.text: Viruses are considered obligate intracellular parasites and are not included in Whittaker's Five Kingdom classification.
options.explanation: Viruses are indeed not included in the five-kingdom system due to their obligate parasitism and lack of cellular structure.

options.text: Viruses are classified under Kingdom Protista because they are microscopic.
options.explanation: Viruses are not classified under Kingdom Protista; they are not cellular and do not fit into any of the five kingdoms.

options.text: Viruses are primitive forms of bacteria and are the first step in the evolution of life.
options.explanation: Viruses are distinct from bacteria and other cellular life forms; they are not considered primitive forms of bacteria.

questions.explanation: Viruses are non-cellular entities that only become active inside a host cell. They lack cellular machinery and cannot reproduce independently. Due to their non-cellular nature and distinct mode of existence (obligate parasitism), they were not included in R.H. Whittaker's Five Kingdom classification system, which categorizes cellular life forms.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of organisms belonging to Kingdom Monera?

options.explanation: Kingdom Monera comprises prokaryotic organisms.
Kingdom Monera comprises prokaryotic organisms, which lack a true nucleus.
Most organisms in Kingdom Monera are unicellular.
Kingdom Monera comprises bacteria, which are prokaryotic organisms.

questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera comprises bacteria, which are prokaryotic organisms, meaning they lack a true nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Mycoplasma are unique among prokaryotes because they:

options.explanation: Mycoplasma lack a cell wall.
The unique characteristic of Mycoplasma is the lack of a cell wall, not their metabolic mode.
Mycoplasma are unique among prokaryotes for lacking a cell wall.
Mycoplasma are prokaryotes and do not perform photosynthesis.

questions.explanation: Mycoplasma are the smallest living cells known and are unique among prokaryotes for completely lacking a cell wall.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following organisms are considered 'chief producers' in the oceans?

options.explanation: While dinoflagellates are photosynthetic, they are not considered the chief producers in the oceans.
Euglenoids are not the chief producers in the oceans.
Chrysophytes are the chief producers in the oceans due to their photosynthetic nature.
Slime moulds are not photosynthetic and thus are not chief producers.

questions.explanation: Chrysophytes (diatoms and desmids) are microscopic and float passively in water currents. They are photosynthetic and are the chief producers in the oceans.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: The Five Kingdom Classification system was proposed by:

options.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus is known for the two-kingdom system.
Ernst Haeckel proposed the three-kingdom system.
R.H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system.
Herbert Copeland proposed a four-kingdom system.

questions.explanation: R.H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification in 1969, classifying organisms into Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Ascospores are endogenously produced in sac-like structures called:

options.explanation: Sporangia are associated with spore production in other fungi, not Ascomycetes.
Basidia are characteristic of Basidiomycetes, not Ascomycetes.
Asci are the sac-like structures where ascospores are produced in Ascomycetes.
Conidia are a type of asexual spore, not related to ascospores.

questions.explanation: Ascospores are sexual spores characteristic of Ascomycetes (sac fungi). They are produced inside a sac-like structure called an ascus (plural: asci).
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: An organism possessing a protein-rich layer called pellicle instead of a cell wall, and having two flagella (one short and one long), belongs to which group?

options.explanation: Dinoflagellates have cell walls and are characterized by their flagella arrangement but do not match the description given.
Euglenoids match the description given, having a pellicle and two flagella of different lengths.
Diatoms have cell walls made of silica and do not match the description.
Slime moulds do not have the characteristics described.

questions.explanation: Euglenoids, such as Euglena, are characterized by the absence of a cell wall, instead having a flexible protein-rich layer called a pellicle. They typically possess two flagella of different lengths.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Fungi are primarily heterotrophic and obtain nutrients by:

options.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic and do not perform photosynthesis.
Fungi do not obtain their nutrients through chemosynthesis.
Fungi obtain nutrients through absorptive nutrition.
Fungi do not ingest their food; they secrete enzymes and absorb the nutrients.

questions.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic and obtain their nutrients by secreting digestive enzymes onto their food source and then absorbing the digested organic molecules. This is known as absorptive nutrition.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: All members of Kingdom Protista are eukaryotic. However, one group within Protista is considered to be a connecting link between plants and animals due to specific characteristics. Identify this group.

options.explanation: Chrysophytes are primarily photosynthetic and do not exhibit the mix of plant and animal characteristics to the same extent as Euglenoids.
Dinoflagellates are primarily marine plankton and do not serve as a connecting link between plants and animals in the same way Euglenoids do.
Euglenoids exhibit characteristics of both plants and animals, making them a connecting link.
Protozoans are heterotrophic and do not have the plant-like characteristics seen in Euglenoids.

questions.explanation: Euglenoids show characteristics of both plants (presence of chloroplasts for photosynthesis) and animals (lack of cell wall, presence of pellicle, and heterotrophic mode of nutrition in the absence of light). This makes them a connecting link.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Viruses are considered obligate parasites. Reason (R): Viruses lack their own cellular machinery and can only reproduce inside a host cell.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason provided correctly explains why viruses are obligate parasites.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason provided does explain why viruses are obligate parasites.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason provided is true and explains the assertion correctly.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason explains the assertion.

questions.explanation: Viruses are indeed obligate parasites because they are acellular and cannot carry out life processes or reproduce independently. They must infect a host cell and utilize its machinery to replicate, which is precisely why they are obligate parasites.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: A scientist observes a single-celled organism under a microscope. It has a well-defined nucleus, chloroplasts, and a cell wall made of cellulose. It reproduces both sexually and asexually. To which kingdom would this organism most likely belong based on these characteristics?

options.explanation: Monera is ruled out because the organism has a well-defined nucleus (eukaryotic).
The characteristics described fit those of some members of the kingdom Protista, such as certain algae.
Fungi is ruled out because it has chloroplasts and a cellulose cell wall (fungi have chitin cell walls and are heterotrophic).
Plantae typically consists of multicellular organisms, although some primitive plants are unicellular. However, the combination of characteristics points more towards Protista.

questions.explanation: The combination of being single-celled, having a nucleus, chloroplasts, and cellulose cell wall, and diverse reproduction strongly points to Protista, which is a diverse group of mostly single-celled eukaryotes, including photosynthetic ones like algae with cellulose cell walls.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following kingdoms consists exclusively of prokaryotic organisms?

options.explanation: Protista is a kingdom that includes eukaryotic organisms.
Fungi are heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms.
The Kingdom Monera includes all bacteria and blue-green algae (cyanobacteria), which are prokaryotic organisms.
Plantae are multicellular and eukaryotic organisms.

questions.explanation: The Kingdom Monera includes all bacteria and blue-green algae (cyanobacteria), which are prokaryotic organisms lacking a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: The cell wall of fungi is primarily composed of:

options.explanation: Cellulose is a component of plant cell walls.
Peptidoglycan is a component of bacterial cell walls.
Hemicellulose is a component of plant cell walls.
Chitin is a complex polysaccharide that makes up the cell walls of fungi.

questions.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms, and their cell walls are characteristically made up of chitin, a complex polysaccharide.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a protozoan protist that moves using pseudopodia?

options.explanation: Paramecium uses cilia for movement.
Euglena uses flagella for movement.
Amoeba uses pseudopodia for movement and feeding.
Diatoms are non-motile or glide.

questions.explanation: Amoeba is a well-known example of a protozoan, specifically a sarcodine, which belongs to the Kingdom Protista and uses pseudopodia for movement and feeding.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Organisms known as 'chief producers in oceans' due to their significant contribution to photosynthesis belong to which group?

options.explanation: Dinoflagellates are a type of protist, but not the chief producers in oceans.
Euglenoids are a type of protist, but not the chief producers in oceans.
Diatoms are considered the chief producers in oceans due to their significant contribution to photosynthesis.
Slime moulds are a type of protist, but not the chief producers in oceans.

questions.explanation: Diatoms are microscopic photosynthetic protists that are found abundantly in marine and freshwater environments and are considered the chief producers in oceans.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which characteristic is unique to Kingdom Fungi among the five kingdoms in terms of its body structure?

options.explanation: Other kingdoms, such as Plantae and Monera, also have cell walls.
Other kingdoms, such as Animalia and some Protista, are also heterotrophic.

options.text: Body composed of hyphae and mycelium
options.explanation: The filamentous structure of hyphae and their network called mycelium are distinct morphological features characteristic of most fungi.
All kingdoms, except Monera, are eukaryotic.

questions.explanation: While other kingdoms may have cell walls (Plantae, Monera) or be heterotrophic (Animalia, some Protista, Monera), and all are eukaryotes (except Monera); the filamentous structure of hyphae and their network called mycelium are distinct morphological features characteristic of most fungi.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: A microorganism is observed to be unicellular, eukaryotic, and capable of both photosynthesis and heterotrophic nutrition depending on the presence or absence of light. To which kingdom would it most likely belong?

options.explanation: Monera is a kingdom of prokaryotic organisms.
The ability to perform both photosynthesis and heterotrophic nutrition is a characteristic feature of certain protists, such as Euglena.
Fungi are typically multicellular and heterotrophic.
Plantae are multicellular and photosynthetic.

questions.explanation: The description of being unicellular and eukaryotic immediately points away from Monera (prokaryotic). Fungi are typically multicellular (except yeast) and heterotrophic (absorptive), while Plantae are multicellular and photosynthetic. The ability to perform both photosynthesis and heterotrophic nutrition (mixotrophic) is a characteristic feature of certain protists, such as Euglena.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: In the five-kingdom classification system, organisms primarily responsible for decomposition and nutrient cycling by breaking down dead organic matter are found predominantly in which two kingdoms?

options.explanation: Plantae are not typically decomposers.
While some protists and animals may contribute to decomposition, they are not the primary decomposers.
Fungi and bacteria are the primary decomposers in ecosystems.
Plantae are not typically decomposers, although some fungi are.

questions.explanation: Fungi are well-known decomposers (saprophytes), and many bacteria (Kingdom Monera) also play a crucial role as decomposers, breaking down organic matter and recycling nutrients in ecosystems.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Archaebacteria is INCORRECT?

options.text: They live in some of the most harsh habitats.
options.explanation: Archaebacteria are known to thrive in extreme environments.

options.text: They have a different cell wall structure from other bacteria.
options.explanation: Archaebacteria have a unique cell wall structure.

options.text: They are often found in the guts of ruminant animals.
options.explanation: Some Archaebacteria are found in the guts of ruminant animals.

options.text: They have peptidoglycan in their cell walls.
options.explanation: Archaebacteria lack peptidoglycan in their cell walls, which distinguishes them from other bacteria.

questions.explanation: Archaebacteria are characterized by their ability to thrive in extreme conditions and for having a distinct cell wall structure that lacks peptidoglycan.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Viruses are not included in the five-kingdom classification system. Reason (R): Viruses lack a cellular structure and are obligate intracellular parasites, existing as a living entity only inside a host cell.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is a correct explanation for the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, and the reason explains it.

questions.explanation: The five-kingdom classification is based on cellular organization, mode of nutrition, and other characteristics of cellular life forms. Viruses are acellular and do not have their own cellular machinery, requiring a host cell to replicate, which is why they are not classified under any of the five kingdoms.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: A scientist discovers a new organism. Microscopic examination reveals it is multicellular, eukaryotic, and has a cell wall. Further tests show that it lacks chlorophyll and obtains nutrients by absorbing organic matter from its surroundings. Based on these characteristics, this organism should be classified under:

options.explanation: Plantae are photosynthetic and have chlorophyll.
Animalia lack cell walls.
The characteristics match those of Kingdom Fungi.
While some protists may have cell walls, the combination of characteristics points more specifically to Kingdom Fungi.

questions.explanation: The combination of multicellular, eukaryotic, cell wall presence, and heterotrophic (absorptive) nutrition points directly to Kingdom Fungi.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of organisms belonging to the kingdom Monera?

options.explanation: This is a characteristic of eukaryotic cells, not prokaryotic cells.
Most Monera are unicellular.
Monera includes prokaryotic organisms like bacteria and archaea.
Chloroplasts are found in plant cells and some protists, not in Monera.

questions.explanation: Monera includes prokaryotic organisms like bacteria and archaea, which lack a defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: In the five-kingdom classification system, which kingdom includes organisms that are eukaryotic, autotrophic, and mostly multicellular?

options.explanation: Monera includes prokaryotic organisms, not eukaryotic organisms.
Protista includes both autotrophic and heterotrophic organisms, and may be unicellular or multicellular.
Fungi are heterotrophic, not autotrophic.
Plantae consists of eukaryotic, multicellular, autotrophic organisms (plants) that perform photosynthesis.

questions.explanation: Plantae consists of eukaryotic, multicellular, autotrophic organisms (plants) that perform photosynthesis.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following groups is NOT included in Whittaker’s five-kingdom classification?

options.explanation: Monera is one of the five kingdoms in Whittaker’s classification.
Protista is one of the five kingdoms in Whittaker’s classification.
Animalia is one of the five kingdoms in Whittaker’s classification.
Viruses are not included in Whittaker’s five-kingdom classification because they are acellular and do not fit the criteria of any of the five kingdoms.

questions.explanation: Viruses are not included in Whittaker’s five-kingdom classification because they are acellular and do not fit the criteria of any of the five kingdoms.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Assertion (A): Fungi are classified under the kingdom Fungi in the five-kingdom system. Reason (R): Fungi are heterotrophic, eukaryotic organisms that absorb nutrients from their surroundings.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion is true as fungi are placed in their own kingdom. The reason is also true and correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true, as fungi are heterotrophic, eukaryotic organisms that absorb nutrients from their surroundings.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true, as fungi are classified under the kingdom Fungi in the five-kingdom system.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true as fungi are placed in their own kingdom. The reason is also true and correctly explains the assertion.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a kingdom that includes both unicellular and multicellular organisms?

options.explanation: Plantae mostly includes multicellular organisms.
Animalia mostly includes multicellular organisms.
Protista includes both unicellular organisms (e.g., Amoeba) and multicellular organisms (e.g., some algae).
Fungi mostly includes multicellular organisms, but some are unicellular.

questions.explanation: Protista includes both unicellular organisms (e.g., Amoeba) and multicellular organisms (e.g., some algae).
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: A student observed an organism under a microscope and noted the following characteristics: It has a cell wall made of chitin, it is heterotrophic and absorbs nutrients from dead organic matter, and it reproduces by spores. Which kingdom does this organism belong to?

options.explanation: Plantae includes autotrophic organisms, not heterotrophic organisms.
Protista includes both autotrophic and heterotrophic organisms, but does not typically have a chitinous cell wall.
The organism described has a chitinous cell wall, is heterotrophic, and reproduces by spores, all of which are characteristics of fungi.
Monera includes prokaryotic organisms, not eukaryotic organisms with a chitinous cell wall.

questions.explanation: The organism described has a chitinous cell wall, is heterotrophic, and reproduces by spores, all of which are characteristics of fungi.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is a key difference between the kingdoms Protista and Monera?

options.text: Protista includes only multicellular organisms, while Monera includes only unicellular organisms.
options.explanation: Both Protista and Monera include unicellular organisms.

options.text: Protista organisms are always photosynthetic, while Monera organisms are always heterotrophic.
options.explanation: Protista includes both autotrophic and heterotrophic organisms, and Monera includes both autotrophic and heterotrophic organisms.

options.text: Protista organisms are eukaryotic, while Monera organisms are prokaryotic.
options.explanation: Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms, whereas Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms.

options.text: Protista includes only animals, while Monera includes only plants.
options.explanation: Protista includes both plant-like and animal-like organisms, and Monera includes bacteria.

questions.explanation: Protista consists of eukaryotic organisms, whereas Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a criterion used by Whittaker for the five-kingdom classification?

options.explanation: Cell structure is one of the criteria used by Whittaker for the five-kingdom classification.
Mode of nutrition is one of the criteria used by Whittaker for the five-kingdom classification.
Level of organization is one of the criteria used by Whittaker for the five-kingdom classification.
Whittaker’s classification is based on cell structure, mode of nutrition, level of organization, and thallus organization, but not specifically on the presence of chlorophyll.

questions.explanation: Whittaker’s classification is based on cell structure, mode of nutrition, level of organization, and thallus organization, but not specifically on the presence of chlorophyll.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: Which kingdom includes organisms that are mostly saprophytic, reproduce by spores, and have a cell wall made of chitin?

options.explanation: Plantae includes autotrophic organisms, not saprophytic organisms.
Fungi are saprophytic, reproduce by spores, and have chitinous cell walls.
Protista includes both autotrophic and heterotrophic organisms, but does not typically have a chitinous cell wall.
Animalia includes heterotrophic organisms, but does not typically have a chitinous cell wall or reproduce by spores.

questions.explanation: Fungi are saprophytic, reproduce by spores, and have chitinous cell walls.
questions.subject: maha11-biology

questions.question: In the five-kingdom classification system, which kingdom includes organisms that are heterotrophic, lack a cell wall, and are capable of locomotion?

options.explanation: Plantae includes autotrophic organisms, not heterotrophic organisms.
Fungi have a cell wall made of chitin.
Some Protista have a cell wall, and not all are capable of locomotion.
Animalia includes heterotrophic organisms that lack a cell wall and are capable of locomotion.

questions.explanation: Animalia includes heterotrophic organisms that lack a cell wall and are capable of locomotion.
questions.subject: maha11-biology
